macos.fallback: no CPUID on arm64: the sysctl is the readable negative; container is always no

windows.fallback: container not read: always unknown, windows:virtualization:container:not_read; an ARM64 build has no CPUID and reads unknown (windows:virtualization:cpuid:unavailable) unless SMBIOS names a VM vendor, and does not detect a Hyper-V or VBS host; no ARM64 build ships, and the x64 agent on a Windows-on-ARM device reads whatever CPUID the emulation presents (not measured)

linux.fallback: Windows-only: WSL distributions are a Windows feature

macos.fallback: Windows-only: WSL distributions are a Windows feature

windows.fallback: a profile whose hive was reached by neither arm is counted and reported on its own profile row, never read as having no distributions; a registry link planted at the Lxss key or at a distribution key is detected and reported (windows:virtualization:wsl:lxss_link), never followed; wsl2 counts version-2 distributions and is not a VM count (the utility VM's running state is not read); base, VHD and shortcut paths, SIDs, uids and hive mount names are never emitted; package version - means unavailable; the offline mount calls have no deadline (the walk is bounded in work, not in time: at most 512 profiles are mounted per dispatch)
windows.mechanism: Reg*W reads of HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Lxss\\MSI, the HKLM ProfileList (profile SIDs and folder paths; no privilege) and each local profile's Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Lxss key through the shared with_user_hive ladder (loaded HKU hive first, else a guarded offline NTUSER.DAT mount under SeBackup/SeRestore and the process-wide offline-hive lock); no subprocess

caveats: **Unreadable is never bare metal.** A host-decision source (SMBIOS, CPUID or OS hint) that fails to read, or a machine with no CPUID (ARM) and no other readable "not virtual" answer, reads `unknown` with the reason, not `bare_metal`. The cost is that some real bare-metal ARM hosts read `unknown`; the benefit is that a refused host-decision read can never be reported as a physical machine. Even a clean `bare_metal` means only that no virtualization signal was seen: a hypervisor that masks both CPUID and SMBIOS reads `bare_metal` (caveat 4).

**A KVM host reads `bare_metal`; a Xen dom0 reads `guest`/`xen`.** The kind describes what the OS the agent runs on is running under. A Linux KVM host's own CPUID is not virtualised, so it is not detected as a hypervisor host. A Xen dom0 is itself a Xen guest: the hypervisor bit is set, the signature is `XenVMMXenVMM` and `/sys/hypervisor/type` says `xen`, so it reads `guest` with vendor `xen`. Only the Windows Hyper-V root partition is reported as `host_with_hypervisor`.

**Container membership is best effort.** An LXD, Incus or systemd-nspawn system container shows the same cgroup path as a host, so the plugin also reads the type systemd records in `/run/systemd/container`. On cgroup v2 an agent inside a cgroup namespace sees `0::/` whatever it runs in, and a host whose init places the agent at the cgroup root reads the same; both are `unknown` (`linux:virtualization:container:cgroup_root_opaque`) unless a marker file or the systemd record answers, never `no`. A container without a marker file or systemd record (a serverless or hand-rolled runtime) can read `no` when its readable, non-root cgroup path has no recognised runtime signature. Windows containers are not read: the row is always `unknown` with `windows:virtualization:container:not_read`. macOS always reports `no`.

**A customised Hyper-V guest can read as a host.** SMBIOS beats the root-partition bit, so a Hyper-V guest whose SMBIOS strings were changed to a non-VM vendor and which is granted CreatePartitions reads `host_with_hypervisor`. Nested virtualization with a custom SMBIOS is the only known case. In the same way a hypervisor operator who masks both the CPUID hypervisor bit and the SMBIOS strings makes a guest read `bare_metal`; the rows are facts as the machine presents them, not attestation. The `wsl` rows are weaker still, because they are what each user's own hive asserts: the `Lxss` subtree is writable by the user it belongs to, so a `distribution` row is that user's claim, not evidence of what is installed and not tamper evidence, and `DistributionName` and `Flavor` are free text that can carry a personal name (only an e-mail shape is redacted). The keys are opened with `REG_OPTION_OPEN_LINK`, so a registry link planted as `Lxss` or as a `{GUID}` child opens as the link object and is never followed; one probe of each opened key for the `SymbolicLinkValue` marker then detects it and reports `lxss_link` (a link at `Lxss` leaves the profile unread, a link at a `{GUID}` child is an `unknown` row), so a planted link is never a clean result. A plain key that holds a decoy value of that name reads the same way: constrained, never fail-open. The flag and the probe cover the last key of each open only, so a link planted at an ancestor (`Software` through `CurrentVersion`, which the user must delete and recreate in their own hive, breaking their own profile) is still followed within whatever the kernel's hive trust rule allows, exposing at most the five value names this walk reads (`DefaultDistribution` under `Lxss`, and `DistributionName`, `Version`, `State` and `Flavor` under the GUID-shaped children).

**Cloud-metadata and runtime detection are out of scope.** The plugin does not query a cloud metadata service, and the running state of the WSL utility VM and of its distributions is not read (`wsl` lists what is installed for each user, not what is running). `vendor` is the virtualization platform the SMBIOS table, the CPUID signature or the macOS model names, never the cloud account or instance: it is `aws`, `gce`, `alibaba`, `openstack` or `nutanix` where SMBIOS names one of those platforms, otherwise the hypervisor token (`qemu`, `hyperv`, `kvm` and so on), or `other` where none of them names a listed platform. A product name containing `.metal` (an AWS bare-metal instance type) reads as hardware.

definitions.description: Reports whether this device is a virtual machine, which hypervisor it runs under and whether the agent itself runs in a container, as facts only. The kind separates a guest from a Windows host that merely runs Hyper-V, VBS or WSL2 (host_with_hypervisor), and from bare_metal, which means no virtualization signal was seen, not proof of physical hardware: a Linux KVM host reads bare_metal, a Xen dom0 reads guest with vendor xen, and an ARM machine with no readable negative signal reads unknown. A host-decision source (SMBIOS, CPUID, OS hint) that cannot be read never reads as bare_metal: the kind is unknown and the reason is on the status row and in the host row's source field; a failed container read makes the status constrained. A leading status row states whether the read was complete: constrained means a source could not be read (a refused read stays refused until permissions change), unsupported means the leg threw. Container membership is best effort: a container without a marker file or systemd record can read no when its readable, non-root cgroup path has no recognised runtime signature, and Windows does not read it.

Lists the Windows Subsystem for Linux distributions installed for each local user profile: the account (the profile folder name), the distribution name, its WSL version (1 or 2), its install state, whether it is that user's default and its flavor. A profile that is not logged on is read through the same guarded offline hive mount the per-user software inventory uses (SeBackupPrivilege and SeRestorePrivilege, already held by the agent; the mount changes that hive's sequence number and hash, #4977). This is per-user data (account and distribution names), so it requires an administrator or an approval. A summary row counts the distributions, how many are WSL 2 (not a VM count: every WSL 2 distribution shares one utility VM whose running state is not read), the profiles read, the profiles whose hive could not be reached and the WSL package version. A profile whose hive was not reached, or whose mount could not be released, is reported on its own profile row; the status row is constrained whenever anything was not read in full, and a registry link planted at the Lxss key or at a distribution key is reported rather than followed. Install paths, disk image paths, SIDs, user ids and mount names are never reported.

description: Virtualization facts: VM or not, which hypervisor, container membership, WSL distributions
how_it_works:
`host` reports whether this device is a virtual machine, which hypervisor it runs under, and whether the agent itself runs in a container, as facts only. It changes nothing and spawns nothing. The first row is always a `status` row saying whether the read was complete, then one `host` row (`is_virtual`, `kind`, `vendor`, `product`, `source`, `confidence`) and one `container` row. `kind` is `guest`, `host_with_hypervisor`, `bare_metal` or `unknown`; a container on a VM reports both facts, because `container` is its own row and not a `kind` value.

The decision is one table in `virtualization_parsers.hpp`, fed by what each OS shell reads. Linux reads CPUID (x86), the DMI `sys_vendor` and `product_name` attributes, `/sys/hypervisor/type`, the marker files `/.dockerenv` and `/run/.containerenv`, the container type systemd records in `/run/systemd/container` (how an LXD, Incus or systemd-nspawn system container is told from a host, because its cgroup path looks the same), and the agent's own `/proc/self/cgroup` (not PID 1's, which answers a different question when the PID namespace is shared). The `/run/systemd/container` content is never emitted, only the fact that it named a container; `wsl` and an empty file are ignored, so a WSL2 agent is not turned into a container. macOS reads `kern.hv_vmm_present` and `hw.model`. Windows reads CPUID and the SMBIOS System Information table. A Windows machine running Hyper-V, VBS or WSL2 sets the CPUID hypervisor bit yet is the host, not a guest: when the hypervisor signature is `Microsoft Hv`, the interface signature is `Hv#1` and the maximum leaf reaches `0x40000003`, the Hyper-V root-partition bit (leaf `0x40000003` EBX bit 0, CreatePartitions) separates a host (`host_with_hypervisor`, `is_virtual` no) from a guest. Without that discovery contract the bit is never read.

Precedence: positive identification always beats negative evidence. SMBIOS or the hardware model naming a VM vendor decides first (so VBS nested inside another hypervisor, which sets the root-partition bit, still reads `guest`); then the root-partition bit; then the CPUID hypervisor bit; then a positive OS hint. `bare_metal` is reachable only when no consulted source identifies virtualization, at least one readable source says "not virtual", and no host-decision source (SMBIOS, CPUID, OS hint) failed to read; a failed container read makes the status `constrained` but does not block `bare_metal`. `bare_metal` means no virtualization signal was seen, not proof of physical hardware. Anything else is `unknown`, with the reasons on the status row and in the host row's `source` field.

`wsl` (Windows only) lists the WSL distributions of every local user profile. For each real profile (system accounts are skipped) it reads `Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Lxss` through the shared `with_user_hive` ladder: the loaded `HKU\<SID>` hive first, else the profile's `NTUSER.DAT` mounted offline under the process-wide offline-hive lock with the default-on hive-file guard, the same span `installed_apps.list_per_user` uses. The profile list itself (SIDs and folder paths) comes from `HKLM\...\ProfileList`. Each child key named by a GUID is one distribution (WSL's own non-GUID children such as `InstallStatus` are skipped); only `DistributionName`, `Version`, `State` and `Flavor` are read, plus the per-user `DefaultDistribution` and the machine-wide WSL package `Version` under `HKLM\...\Lxss\MSI`. Every key under the hive root is opened with `REG_OPTION_OPEN_LINK`, and the `Lxss` key and each distribution key are probed once for the `SymbolicLinkValue` marker of a registry link, so a link planted at either is reported (`lxss_link`) and never read through; the machine-wide `...\Lxss\MSI` key is opened the same way but not probed (only an administrator can plant a link there, and it reads as a package version of `-`). The rows are a `status` row, one `summary` row, one `profile` row for each profile that was not reached or whose mount could not be released, and one `distribution` row per distribution, sorted by account then name. Linux and macOS answer one `unsupported` status row. The walk is bounded in work, not in time: one budget per dispatch caps the registry enumeration and value-read calls (4096, the link probes included; opening a key is not counted), a value (4 KiB), rows (1024, which includes the two reserved status and summary rows) and output (256 KiB) across all hives, and each hive is also held to 512 of those calls, 128 rows and 32 KiB so that one hostile hive ends alone. The number of hives mounted is bounded by the profile cap alone, not by the call budget: a dispatch visits at most 512 profiles, so the worst case is 512 serial mount and unload cycles, and a hive with no Lxss key costs no counted call. The lock wait, `RegLoadKeyW` and `RegUnLoadKeyW` have no deadline, exactly as for `installed_apps.list_per_user`. If an unload fails, that profile's `NTUSER.DAT` stays locked and the mount `HKU\YUZU_HIVE_<SID>_...` is left behind: list `HKU` with `reg query HKU`, find the `YUZU_HIVE_*` key (its exact name is in the agent log) and release it with `reg unload HKU\<mount>`. Until then that user's next logon gets a temporary profile, and a repeat `wsl` dispatch reports the profile as `mount_failed`. The only automatic cleanup is the Echo plugin's start-up sweep of `YUZU_HIVE_*` mounts, so an agent without Echo loaded needs the manual step. The decision, the bounds and the fake-registry tests are in `virtualization_wsl_parsers.hpp`.

### What you can decide with it

| Question | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Is this device a VM? | Yes: `is_virtual` yes, no or unknown, with the evidence source and a confidence. | Yes, from `kern.hv_vmm_present` and the model name. | Yes, from CPUID and SMBIOS. |
| Which hypervisor? | The CPUID signature, a DMI vendor or `/sys/hypervisor/type`. | `apple` for a `VirtualMac*` model, `vmware` for a VMware model string, otherwise `other`. | The CPUID signature or the SMBIOS vendor. |
| Is the agent in a container? | `yes` on a marker file, a container type in `/run/systemd/container` or a container cgroup path; `no` only when all of those are readable and absent and the cgroup names a real path (a container without a marker file or systemd record can also read `no` when its readable, non-root cgroup path has no recognised runtime signature, caveat 3); otherwise `unknown`. | Always `no`. | Not read: always `unknown`. |
| Is this a Hyper-V, VBS or WSL2 host? | A WSL2 guest reads `guest` `hyperv`. | n/a | Yes on x86: `host_with_hypervisor`, `is_virtual` no. Not detected on ARM64, which has no CPUID. |
| Which WSL distributions does each user have? | `wsl`: one `unsupported` row. | `wsl`: one `unsupported` row. | `wsl`: per local profile, the distribution name, WSL version, state, default and flavor, including profiles that are logged off. |

### Diagrams

#### How the kind is decided

The order matters: a positive identification is never outranked by a negative or missing signal, and an unreadable host-decision source (SMBIOS, CPUID, OS hint) can never be read as "not virtual".

outputs_note:
Every row is pipe-delimited and field 0 is the row kind; `-` is an absent value. The first row of a `host` dispatch is always `status|host|<supported\|constrained\|unsupported>|<reason or ->`. The `host` row has seven fields: `host|<yes\|no\|unknown>|<guest\|host_with_hypervisor\|bare_metal\|unknown>|<vendor>|<product>|<source>|<high\|medium\|low>`. `vendor` is the virtualization platform (`kvm`, `hyperv`, `vmware`, `xen`, `virtualbox`, `parallels`, `bhyve`, `qemu`, `acrn`, `aws`, `gce`, `alibaba`, `openstack`, `nutanix`, `apple` or `other`) for a guest or host, and the hardware manufacturer for `bare_metal` and `unknown`. `source` is the evidence that decided the kind (`cpuid`, `smbios`, `sysctl` or `sys_hypervisor`); when the kind is `unknown` it carries the joined host-decision reason tokens instead (container read failures stay on the container row), so the row an operator reads explains itself. The `container` row is `container|<yes\|no\|unknown>|<evidence or reason>`. Every OS-supplied value (DMI and SMBIOS strings, the hardware model) is scrubbed (NUL and malformed UTF-8 become `?`) and escaped for the server's pipe grammar.

`wsl` rows (Windows). The first row is `status|wsl|<supported\|constrained\|unsupported>|<reason or ->`, then `summary|<distributions>|<wsl2>|<profiles_read>|<profiles_not_loaded>|<package_version or ->`. `distributions` is the number of `distribution` rows emitted. `wsl2` counts version-2 distributions and is NOT a VM count: every WSL 2 distribution shares one utility VM whose running state is readable only through `wsl.exe` or the WSL service, which this plugin does not call. `profiles_read` counts the hives whose Lxss key was read or found absent (an absent key counts: that profile has no WSL); a cap that stops the read inside the key still counts it and is reported by its token. `profiles_not_loaded` counts the profiles whose hive was reached by neither the loaded hive nor the offline mount, including `.bak` entries and invalid SIDs, and the profiles never reached because a dispatch-wide limit stopped the walk (those get no `profile` row: the output budget was spent). `profiles_read` + `profiles_not_loaded` need not equal the profile count: a hive that was reached but whose Lxss key could not be opened, or is a registry link, is in neither, and is reported only by its `hive_access_denied`, `hive_open_failed` or `lxss_link` token (a token carries no account). `package_version` is `-` when unavailable or over 64 bytes. A `profile` row, `profile|<account or ->|<outcome>|<detail or ->`, is emitted only for a profile that was not reached or whose mount could not be released; `outcome` is one of `not_found`, `privilege_missing`, `mount_failed`, `access_denied`, `file_refused`, `unload_failed`, `backup_skipped` or `sid_invalid`, and `detail` is the hive-file guard's reason verbatim for `file_refused` (`hive_path_unc`, `hive_identity_changed` and the others in `agents/shared/win_hive_file_guard.hpp`) and `-` otherwise. An `unload_failed` row means the offline mount was left behind and keeps `NTUSER.DAT` locked until `reg unload HKU\<mount>` succeeds (find the `YUZU_HIVE_*` key with `reg query HKU`; until then that user's next logon gets a temporary profile and a repeat dispatch reports the profile as `mount_failed`, and only the Echo plugin's start-up sweep cleans up on its own, see How it works); the mount name embeds the SID, so it is written to the agent log only and never to a row. A `distribution` row is `distribution|<account or ->|<name>|<1\|2\|unknown>|<installed\|installing\|uninstalling\|converting\|exporting\|compacting\|state_<n>\|unknown>|<yes\|no>|<flavor or ->`; `account` is the profile folder name, never the SID, and `yes` marks that account's default distribution. The state names follow the WSL service's own state enum (the public WSL source, `_LxssDistributionState`): `installed` is 1, `installing` 3, `uninstalling` 4, `converting` 5, `exporting` 6 and `compacting` 7; 0 (invalid), 2 (running, a session state) and anything past 7 print as `state_<n>`, and only `installed` has been seen on a measured host. A distribution whose key could not be opened, or is a registry link, is a row with `-` for the name, `unknown` for version and state, and its default flag. Account, distribution name and flavor are e-mail redacted by value (`[redacted-email]`) and every field is scrubbed and escaped for the pipe grammar.

privileges.grant: `host`: None: CPUID is an unprivileged instruction and the SMBIOS table is read through `GetSystemFirmwareTable`. `wsl`: None beyond what the agent account already holds: the action uses the same `with_user_hive` span `installed_apps.list_per_user` already uses. The `HKLM` ProfileList (profile SIDs and folder paths) and the WSL package `Version` need no privilege, nor does a loaded `HKU\<SID>` hive; a logged-off profile's `NTUSER.DAT` is mounted offline with `SeBackupPrivilege` and `SeRestorePrivilege`, already held by the agent account and enabled only inside the offline arm, under the process-wide offline-hive lock and the default-on hive-file guard
privileges.if_refused: `host`: `CONSTRAINED` / partial with `windows:virtualization:smbios:<cause>`; the kind is `unknown` unless CPUID or a decoded Type 1 already identifies the machine. `wsl`: a hardened install that strips the two privileges still reads every logged-on profile; a logged-off one is a `profile` row with outcome `privilege_missing` and the token `windows:virtualization:wsl:hive_privilege_missing`. A refused hive file is `file_refused` with the guard's reason, a refused live root `access_denied`; none is read as having no distributions
privileges.measured: `host`: Measured 2026-11-07 on a Windows 11 host with Hyper-V, VBS and WSL2 enabled, from an elevated interactive session (not LocalSystem): CPUID and the firmware table both answered; whether an unelevated caller gets the table was not measured. `wsl`: Measured 2026-11-08 on the same host as `host`, as LocalSystem (a scheduled task, the agent's own identity), with the native MSVC build. The loaded `HKU` hive of the logged-on profile was read live (the sample); no real account on that host was logged off with a Lxss key, so the offline arm was measured on a disposable local account that had never logged on and was logged off: its `NTUSER.DAT` was mounted and read through `SeBackupPrivilege` and `SeRestorePrivilege`, a registry link planted at the `Lxss` key or at a distribution key was reported as `lxss_link` and never read through (no decoy row appeared), a mount that could not be unloaded gave `hive_unload_failed` with the mount name only in the agent log, and a leftover `YUZU_HIVE_*` mount gave `hive_mount_failed` on the next run; a planted link was not followed by the kernel across hives from a user hive either. The account was removed afterwards

privileges.grant: None: both sysctls answer an unprivileged caller
privileges.if_refused: `CONSTRAINED` / partial with `macos:virtualization:hv_vmm_present:unreadable` or `macos:virtualization:hw_model:unreadable`; the kind is `unknown` unless the other sysctl still identifies a guest
privileges.measured: The sample was captured as an unprivileged user, not under the LaunchDaemon account
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon (root under the shipped LaunchDaemon today, `docs/agent-privilege-model.md`)

privileges.grant: None: the DMI attributes and `/run/systemd/container` read are world-readable; the root-only `product_serial` and `product_uuid` are never read
privileges.if_refused: `CONSTRAINED` / partial; a refused host-decision source (SMBIOS, CPUID, OS hint) reports `linux:virtualization:<source>:<cause>` and the kind `unknown` (or the kind another source already established), never `bare_metal`; a refused container read reports `linux:virtualization:container:<cause>`, constrains the status and does not block `bare_metal`
privileges.measured: Measured 2026-11-07 inside a WSL2 distribution as root (not the packaged `yuzu-agent` account): `/run/systemd/container` is mode 0644 root:root under a 0755 `/run/systemd`; that kernel exposes no `/sys/class/dmi/id` or `/sys/hypervisor`, so the DMI modes were not measured and the host answer came from CPUID alone
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon, dedicated unprivileged account (`yuzu-agent` on the packaged unit), never root by design (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`)

result_status.when: every consulted source was read and the kind is established, or the container row is `unknown` by declaration (Windows: `windows:virtualization:container:not_read`) or by classification (`linux:virtualization:container:cgroup_root_opaque`); both appear on the container row only, never in the status provenance

Linux: a DMI attribute or `/sys/hypervisor/type` could not be read. `<cause>` is `permission_denied`, `eio`, `eloop`, `enotdir`, `einval`, `not_regular`, `oversized` or `errno_<n>`; a missing file (ENOENT) is a definitive absence, not a failure

No CPUID on this architecture (ARM) and nothing else supplied a readable "not virtual" answer, so the kind is `unknown`; not added when SMBIOS or a hint identifies the machine, nor on macOS when the sysctl answers

Linux: a container marker probe, `/run/systemd/container` or `/proc/self/cgroup` could not be read; the container row is `unknown` unless a marker, the systemd record or a cgroup runtime already answered. A missing `/run/systemd/container` is the normal host case, not a failure
SMBIOS was reported unreadable with no cause token; a defensive fallback so an unknown is never unexplained (no shipped leg produces it today)
macOS: a sysctl could not be read; the kind is `unknown` unless the other sysctl still identifies a guest
Windows: the SMBIOS table walk stopped at a framing fault, the Type 1 structure was malformed, or the firmware-table read failed. A Type 1 decoded before a later fault still identifies a VM vendor

Windows `wsl`: a profile's hive was reached by neither arm (no loaded hive and no profile path; SeBackup/SeRestore could not both be enabled; the offline load or the root re-open failed; a refused live root or Lxss read; the hive-file guard refused the file; a `.bak` ProfileList entry, never mounted; an invalid SID, never accessed). Each is also a `profile` row and counts in `profiles_not_loaded`, except `hive_access_denied` raised by a denied read of the Lxss key itself, which has no row and no count (that profile is in neither summary count)
Windows `wsl`: an offline mount was left behind, whatever else happened to that profile. The distributions already read are kept; the mount name is in the agent log only

Windows `wsl`: the Lxss key could not be opened (other than absent or access denied, which is `hive_access_denied`), its children could not be enumerated (rows read so far are kept), or one distribution key could not be opened (its row carries `-` for the name and `unknown` for version and state)

Windows `wsl`: the Lxss key, or one distribution key, carries a `SymbolicLinkValue` value, which is what a registry link looks like when it is opened as itself (`REG_OPTION_OPEN_LINK`). The link is reported and never read through. A link at Lxss leaves that profile unread, in neither summary count; a link at a distribution key is a row with `-` for the name and `unknown` for version and state. A plain key that holds a decoy value of that name (a REG_SZ, say) reads the same way: constrained, never a clean result

Windows `wsl`: a value could not be read (denied, or it changed between the size probe and the read), had the wrong type or size, or exceeded 4 KiB (never allocated); the field reads `-` or `unknown`. The link-marker probe of a key that failed to answer is also `value_unreadable`: the key is then read as a plain one
Windows `wsl`: the WSL package `Version` was over 64 bytes or the wrong type, or its key or value could not be read; `package_version` is `-`. A missing key is not a failure

Windows `wsl`: the ProfileList could not be opened or enumerated to the end, stopped at 512 profiles with more present, or a profile's record could not be read or its path was present but unusable; the profiles that were enumerated are still read

Windows `wsl`: the dispatch budget (1024 rows, which include the reserved status and summary rows, or 256 KiB of output; 4096 enumeration and value-read calls) stopped the walk; rows and counts cover what was read before it, and profiles after the stop were not accessed (they count in `profiles_not_loaded`, with no row)

Windows `wsl`: one profile's hive reached its own allowance (128 distributions or 32 KiB of rows, or 512 registry calls); the distributions of that hive read before the limit are kept, the rest of it was not read, and the remaining profiles were still read
`wsl` on Linux or macOS: the action is Windows-only and reads nothing; one `unsupported` status row
a leg threw: an `unsupported` status row, reported instead of unwinding across the plugin boundary

stamp.privilege: LocalSystem (elevated; account names replaced with jsmith)

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore, queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`. `host` is also a gathered definition (`crossplatform.virtualization.host`, 3600s TTL); `wsl` is the role-gated definition `windows.virtualization.wsl` (3600s response window; how often it runs is the operator's scheduling).
**Not consumed by** daily-sync, Echo, DEX, or metrics.

**Sensitivity (`host`).** The `host` rows describe the device, not a person: no account, hostname, serial number, UUID or MAC address is emitted. The Linux leg never reads the root-only `product_serial` and `product_uuid`; on Windows the shared SMBIOS walker decodes the Type 1 serial number and UUID in memory, and the plugin never keeps or emits them. The SMBIOS manufacturer and product (or the macOS model) and the virtualization platform can identify the hardware or cloud provider of a device. The container evidence is a marker path or a runtime name, never a container or pod identifier.

**Sensitivity (`wsl`).** The `wsl` rows are per-user data: the account (the profile folder name) and each distribution name are emitted, which can identify a person; an e-mail-shaped account, distribution name or flavor is replaced by `[redacted-email]`, and any other text is emitted after the pipe-grammar scrub (NUL, CR and LF are scrubbed and the field separator is escaped; a personal name that is not an e-mail address is not redacted). Never emitted: install and disk-image paths (`BasePath`, `VhdFileName`, shortcut and terminal-profile paths), the package family name, default user ids, kernel command lines, NAT addresses, the distribution GUID, any SID, and the offline mount name (it embeds the SID; it goes to the agent log only). The action is gated behind `AdminOrApproval` (definition `approval.mode: role-gated`), on by default, and mounting a logged-off profile's hive changes that hive's sequence number and hash (#4977).
**Siblings:** `hardware` (manufacturer, model and serials of the machine) and `device_identity`; this plugin only says whether that machine is virtual.
